newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola ends up on fund, exporter demand.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola ends up on fund, exporter demand.

text.p: Winnipeg Commodity Exchange canola futures ended up on fund and exporter demand, traders said.
"Exporters bought 800 November and funds bought 600," a trader said. "There were late hedges that took us off our highs and RBC-DS bought Sep-Nov at $1 at the close."
November WCE canola crush profit margin fell to -20.98 Tuesday from -19.20 Monday. Sep-Nov spread at $1, Nov-Jan $3, Nov-Mar $3.50. Volume was 3,530 lots, or 70,600 tonnes, with 630 hedges.
Japan bought 4,000 tonnes of canola, sources said.
November canola rose $5.50 to close at $366.40 and January was up $5 to $370.
November flax rose $6.30 to $307.30 on commercial trade.
Alberta Wheat Pool bought October feed wheat up $1.60 to $159.90 as UGG and PCTS sold scale up, traders said. December rose $1.60 to $159.80, sources said. Volume 575 lots.
RBC-DS and commercials bought October western barley up $2.50 at $136.90 and December ended up $2.40 at $139 with UGG selling, traders said.
Oct-Dec spread at $2. Volume was 470 lots.
UGG and RBC-DS bought October peas up US$0.40 at US$167.50 from commercials, a trader said. Volume was 50 lots.
(All values in Canadian dollars per tonne except oats, feed peas.)
